subject: EHR integration: hosting route, SOC2/BAA evidence & next steps
body:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Michael Ramos <michael.ramos@medsync.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@medsync.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jan 2028 14:02:00 -0500
Subject: EHR integration: hosting route, SOC2/BAA evidence & next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the right hosting route for the EHR integration.

Recap (from our conversation):
- Primary constraint: PHI content (patient notes & identifiers) will be sent from MedSync to Redwood for inference.
- Volume estimate: ~120M tokens / month initially; expected to grow with pilot.
- Latency target: sub-300ms p99 for user-facing workflows.
- Primary preference: MedSync security team verbally preferred a private VPC or on-prem option, but procurement asked for SOC2 evidence and a BAA prior to a decision.
- Timeline: pilot kickoff target in late Feb.

Recommended hosting options (pros/cons brief):
1) Private VPC/on-prem: best for full data isolation and KMS control. Requires customer network provisioning (VPN/Cross-connect), KMS integration, and an initial infra validation window. Longest lead but lowest compliance friction.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs in our cloud): offers predictable throughput and keeps data isolated to your committed pool. Faster to stand up than VPC but still requires tenant-level controls and a BAA.
3) Hosted API (shared): fastest onboarding but not ideal for PHI-heavy workload unless you accept additional contractual controls — not our recommendation for this project.

Immediate asks we need from MedSync to narrow the path:
- Confirm whether PHI will persist in logs, or if you require token-level zero retention (yes/no)
- Preferred KMS provider (Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, HashiCorp, customer HSM)
- Network connectivity preference (site-to-site VPN, Azure ExpressRoute, AWS Direct Connect, or allowlist of outbound IPs)
- Procurement timing for the BAA and any required vendor questionnaire (e.g. security questionnaire PDF)

Attachments included with this email: Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2027.pdf, BAA_template_Medsync_v1.docx (attached as stubs). Also attaching a sample network diagram template we use (network_diagram_medsync.png) to help your infra team review.

Proposed next steps:
- Please share answers to the four asks above by EOD Thu (1/26) if possible.
- Customer security sync: Jan 26, 10:00 AM PT — we can include a Solutions Engineer and our infra architect to walk through VPC prerequisites.
- If target is faster standing up, we can scope Dedicated capacity as a fallback while private VPC is provisioned.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for Jan 26.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Michael Ramos <michael.ramos@medsync.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@medsync.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jan 2028 16:12:34 -0500
Subject: Re: EHR integration: hosting route, SOC2/BAA evidence & next steps

Thanks Naomi — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 
- PHI handling: our legal/compliance requires no persistence of identifiable PHI in vendor logs; we prefer token-level zero retention. We will send an excerpt of the legal language for the BAA team.
- Monthly token estimate: closer to 120–150M tokens for pilot, with bursts up to ~400 concurrent requests.
- Preferred KMS: Azure Key Vault (we run in Azure gov for some workloads, but pilot may sit in commercial).
- Network: we prefer a Private VPC with ExpressRoute to avoid public internet egress for PHI. If ExpressRoute is difficult, then a site-to-site VPN is acceptable short-term.

Procurement note: our procurement asked for: SOC2 Type II report, the BAA, an updated vendor security questionnaire (they will send), and an initial network diagram showing where data flows. Can you confirm SOC2 report is current and whether you have a pre-signed BAA?

We can do the security sync on Jan 26 — 10:00 AM PT works for us. I'll ask our security engineer (Priya) to join.

-Michael

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Jan 2028 17:05:12 -0500
Subject: Re: EHR integration: hosting route, SOC2/BAA evidence & next steps

Michael — appreciate the details. Quick responses inline and a slightly more prescriptive ask list so your security team can prepare ahead of the sync: 

- SOC2: attached "Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2027.pdf" — this is our latest SOC2 Type II report covering security and availability controls. The report is current through Q4 2027.
- BAA: attached a pre-populated BAA template (BAA_template_Medsync_v1.docx) we usually use as a starting point. We do not pre-sign BAAs — procurement typically redlines and returns. Happy to accelerate.
- Network diagram: attached network_diagram_medsync.png — this is a template showing how a Private VPC deployment looks end-to-end; we’ll fill in specifics once you share connectivity preference.

Private VPC checklist (what Redwood needs to validate before we can stand up a private environment):
1) Affirmation on token-level log retention (zero retention preferred).
2) List of egress/ingress subnets or acceptance of ExpressRoute/Direct Connect connectivity model.
3) KMS details and owner contact for key exchange and rotation policy.
4) Contact for your infra team for cross-connect/RBAC setup.

If some items take longer, Dedicated capacity is a practical fallback: we can reserve a GPU pool scoped to your tenant and apply the BAA and tenant isolation while we finish the VPC. Performance characteristics are close to Private VPC for inference latency, but full network isolation is better with Private VPC.

I’ll send the calendar invite for Jan 26 10:00 AM PT with our Solutions Engineer (Karthik) and infra architect (Soojin) copied.

Regards,
Naomi

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2027.pdf (stub), BAA_template_Medsync_v1.docx (stub), network_diagram_medsync.png (stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Jan 2028 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: EHR integration: hosting route, SOC2/BAA evidence & next steps

Michael / Naomi — quick technical notes ahead of the security sync: 
- The attached SOC2 report covers the control families your procurement referenced (change control, access control, incident response). We will prepare a short mapping doc for Jan 26 that ties the report sections to the questionnaire items you send.
- Dedicated capacity feasibility: we can provision a reserved GPU pool within 2–3 weeks after contract, and it meets the latency target (p99 ~220–300ms depending on sequence length). If you need strict network egress control (ExpressRoute), Private VPC will be required; Dedicated capacity can be paired with strict tenant-level IAM and encryption-in-transit but still traverses our cloud provider backbone.
- For the VPC path we need an allowlist (CIDR) or an ExpressRoute/Direct Connect contact; please also share the Azure subscription ID if ExpressRoute is used so we can coordinate peerings.
- KMS: Azure Key Vault is supported — we’ll send the key exchange steps in the pre-call package. If you have an HSM, we can support bring-your-own-HSM with additional setup.

Pre-call deliverables (we will send these today):
1) SOC2-to-questionnaire mapping (PDF)
2) Private VPC runbook (high-level steps and expected lead times)
3) Dedicated capacity SLA and sizing worksheet

See you on Jan 26. I’ll include the runbook and mapping in the calendar invite.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
